note: NYULO: does the NYUv2 relative-scatter curve return to its single-task anchor as the dose goes to zero? The four NYUCAP sweeps stop at alpha=0.01, where the joint scatter already sits at 0.83 (m=32) / 0.64 (m=256) of the per-seed single-task anchor, and that shortfall is what makes the scatter half-height crossing return the wrong sign (gamma=-0.77 against the probe's +0.27). Two readings are possible: the anchor is structurally unreachable in this domain, or the grid simply stopped too high. These sweeps extend the same protocol four decades down (alpha = 1e-6 .. 1e-3) so the plateau of the relative-scatter curve is measured rather than assumed. The alpha grid also repeats the NYUCAP points, which makes the overlapping cells a built-in protocol check: they must reproduce xcap_nyu_m*.json to floating-point equality. Protocol identical to NYUCAP (harness MLP, batch 128, 100 epochs, seeds 0-9, cal-warm 4); the single-task anchor is recomputed per seed inside the sweep, so rel_scatter is on the same scale as NYUCAP and R7.
